As the installed nDPI names it. A protocol that carries others - TLS, QUIC, HTTP - takes every application it carries. Suricata matches the names nDPI knows the application by, and its protocol when Suricata reads that protocol itself; one it can tell by neither gets no Suricata rule, and the rest still acts.

Block: a block rule of this plugin's on the application's table, from the source alone and ahead of the rules of Firewall: Rules, so a new connection from there to a server in the table is dropped; the connections nDPI names as the application from there cut, some 10 to 70 seconds after they began - in hardware too, where os-xgs-npu is installed with Cut in hardware on; and a Suricata rule that drops them on their way to the internet in the Intrusion Detection's IPS mode and alerts in its IDS mode - never a connection to the firewall itself or to its own networks. Alert: a Suricata rule that alerts on them, nothing blocked.

Blocked: chosen in Blocked applications. Connections cut: those nDPI named as the application, their pf states killed. Packets stopped: dropped by its block rules on their way to a server in its table, since the firewall's rules were last loaded.

Connections: named by nDPI from their packets since the classifier started. Guessed: named by port or address only, never put in a table. Each connection counts once, in the window it began in.
Cut in hardware is off in XGS: Settings: a connection cut leaves hardware once pf has let go of its state.
Cut in hardware is on in XGS: Settings: a connection cut is dropped on the coprocessor first.

Each application chosen is blocked: a table of its own, as in Application tables, and a block rule of this plugin's on it, ahead of the rules of Firewall: Rules, so a new connection from any interface to a server in the table is dropped - on every port, so another service on the same address is blocked as well. A connection nDPI names as it from its packets is cut once its window is judged, some 10 to 70 seconds after it began: its pf states killed by its two ends and, with Cut in hardware on in os-xgs-npu's XGS: Settings, dropped on the coprocessor first. Its server goes into the table only when the firewall's own resolver gives that address for the name the connection carried, since a device can write any name to any address, and only when nothing named that address, within the address expiry, as an application not blocked; else that connection alone is cut. Those it named earlier and still remembers are cut at Apply. A guess, a connection whose beginning was not seen, and one to the firewall, a host of its internal networks or an address not on the internet - private, shared or unique-local - are never cut. Choosing a protocol that carries others - TLS, QUIC, HTTP, DNS - blocks every application it carries. None chosen, or classifying off: nothing is blocked.

Each rule acts on its application for the devices of its source. Block: a block rule of this plugin's on the application's table, from that source alone and ahead of the rules of Firewall: Rules; the connections nDPI names as the application from there cut, in hardware too where os-xgs-npu is installed; and a Suricata rule. Alert: a Suricata rule alone, which alerts. Every device but those of a source: invert it - a block for all but one device, say.

Each table is an External alias in Firewall: Aliases, for a rule's source or destination: servers nDPI named, each kept until unseen for the address expiry. The table of an application chosen in Blocked applications has a block rule of this plugin's as well, and takes a server only when the firewall's own resolver gives that address for the name its connection carried.

Every device but those of the source: a block for every device except one, say. One item only. An address written by hand leaves out that address alone, not the same device's address of the other family: an alias holding both does.
For your reference; Suricata's alerts carry it too.
How long an address stays in a table once unseen: the Expire of the tables' aliases, carried out by OPNsense's own cron. Seen again, its time starts again.

Name each connection's application with nDPI and keep the servers it names in pf tables, aliases in Firewall: Aliases. It reads a copy of what the firewall sees and changes no traffic.
